from_quote: You have been addressed in the last Friday's paper, by a writer under the signature of Caution
rationale: The piece answers "a writer under the signature of Caution" in "the last Friday's paper"; Caution appeared in the Maryland Journal of Friday, October 12, 1787, four days before this piece.

from_quote: But Caution thinks a petition improper and unnecessary ; because, says he, "your Delegates will move for, and exert themselves to procure, the calling a Convention."
rationale: The paragraph states Caution's argument that a petition is "improper and unnecessary" because the Delegates will move for a Convention, and sets out to answer it.
to_quote: no one would oppose such a petition, although improper and unnecessary, because your Delegates will certainly move for, and exert themselves to procure, the calling a Convention

from_quote: the seeds of reformation are sown in the work itself, and the concurrence of two-thirds of the Congress may, at any time, introduce alterations and amendments
rationale: In the passage of Wilson's speech that the piece quotes, the provision by which "the concurrence of two-thirds of the Congress" may introduce amendments is named so specifically that only Article V fits.
